status_summary: On 2025-05-21 CMS announced it would audit every eligible Medicare Advantage contract in each payment year, finish remaining audits for payment years 2018 to 2024 by early 2026, and use samples of 35 to 200 records per contract. On 2025-09-25 the Northern District of Texas, in Humana v. Becerra, vacated the 2023 RADV final rule's removal of the fee-for-service adjuster, together with its codified extrapolation, on notice-and-comment grounds and remanded it; the government filed a notice of appeal to the Fifth Circuit on 2025-11-21. A CMS memo of 2026-01-27 says HHS will comply with the order while it stands and expects to begin payment year 2020 audits by February 2026. The Fifth Circuit heard argument on 2026-10-05 and no decision was found.

timeline.event: CMS announces it will audit all eligible Medicare Advantage contracts each payment year, complete 2018 to 2024 audits by early 2026, and expand samples to 35 to 200 records.
CMS starts a first payment year 2019 RADV audit batch (second batch 2025-06-25), later extending record deadlines and restoring a five-month window.

timeline.event: Fifth Circuit panel hears oral argument in the government's appeal; no decision reported.

title: Restore Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data validation (RADV) audits
uncertainties: The district court opinion and appellate docket were not opened; the vacatur and appeal rest on law-firm and news summaries, which agree on a 2025-11-21 notice of appeal (the 2025-11-01 date in one lead was not supported). The CMS memo was read as a copy hosted by a trade association. The document calls the RADV rule a Trump-era rule, while the vacated rule was finalized in 2023 from a 2018 proposal. MCIT, MAQI and ACO REACH are not assessed here. Whether payment year 2020 audits began on schedule was not confirmed.
